newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Bosnia peace coordinator Bildt in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Bosnia peace coordinator Bildt in hospital.

text.p: Swedish political Carl Bildt, who is overseeing international peace efforts in Bosnia, was in a Stockholm hospital on Sunday suffering from an infection, a hospital spokeswoman said.

She told Reuters that Bildt, 47, was admitted to Danderyds Hospital in the Swedish capital's northern suburbs on Saturday for tests. It was unclear how long he would remain there and no further details were available.
Bildt, the leader of Sweden's oppositon conservative party, the Moderates, and a former Swedish prime minister, went to hospital suffering from a headache, tiredness and having difficulty speaking.
Swedish newspapers said doctors described his condition as stable.
"Carl Bildt has got what doctors simply call an infection and he is feeling better now," the Moderate's party secretary, Gunnar Hokmark, said.
Bildt returned to Stockholm on Friday for a weekend visit.
He was due to go to London on Sunday and return to Bosnia on Tuesday. None of Bildt's family nor anyone from the Moderates was able to say how these plans would be disrupted.
Bildt was the prime minister from 1991 until 1994 when the country's traditional ruling party, the Social Democrats regained power in a general election.
His work in Bosnia as the major power's High Representative has earned him international respect.
Bildt has already said that this year he will give up his position in Bosnia and return to Sweden to lead the Moderates into the next general election in September 1998.
